newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain's Hogg sees long haul to end EU beef ban.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Hogg sees long haul to end EU beef ban.

text.p: The European Union will not be asked to ease a worldwide ban on British beef exports until early spring, Britain's farm minister Douglas Hogg said on Tuesday.
"I would not say it will take years but we have got quite a long way to travel," Hogg said in a British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) television interview.
The EU will only be asked to start lifting the ban after Britain has submitted a written proposal to the European Commission in January or February, he added.
It will then have to be scrutinised by the EU Standing Veterinary Committee which will make a recommendation.

"Clearly the ball will now be in the court of some other member states. A working proposal will be put to the Commission and at that point member states will have to fashion their responses to our programme," he said.

Hogg blamed farmers in Britain for delaying the introduction of the selective cull of an additional 100,000 cattle which is the final plank in the July Florence agreement on eradicating mad cow disease in Britain.

"There has been a decided change in the attitude of the farming community. Until October they were against a selective cull and it would have been difficult to impose a selective cull that they were all opposing," he explained.

There is no timetable for the lifting or easing of the export ban imposed in March following an announcement by the British government that Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy could be linked to the human equivalent Creutzfeldt-Jacob Disease.
"We are coming forward with our proposition which will include a proposal for certified herds which we hope will be the first step," Hogg said.
Irish farm minister Ivan Yates said on arrival for the second day of the farm ministers' meeting, "This is an important step forward and it allows a new phase to begin."
"The final stage of the Florence agreement is late but it is better late than never. A number of member states are very anxious to see the final stage of implementation."
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said, "I am waiting to see what Mr Hogg has to say."
